In detail

West Midlands Police recorded 280 crimes inside this ward's official boundary over the 3 months to July 2026 — an average of 5.4 per 1,000 residents a month, the 17th highest rate of Coventry's 18 wards. The daytime score here is driven by vehicle crime (14), burglary (7), shoplifting (1); the evening/night score by violent crime (41), public order (6), anti social behaviour (5). Those two scores are split by offence type, not by clock time — the police feed records no time of day, so day and night here mean the kinds of crime typical of each, not counts of incidents observed then. Rated against the average of the city's own wards, never against another city.

Frequently asked questions

Is Bablake safe?

Wandroz currently rates Bablake in Coventry as roughly average compared to other neighbourhoods in Coventry during the day and relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Coventry at night. This rating is derived from West Midlands Police street-level crime records published at data.police.uk — an official statistic, not an assessment. High-footfall tourist, transit or shopping areas can read higher on this kind of measure without that meaning elevated risk per visit, since these statistics are normalised against registered residents rather than footfall — see the note on this page and the methodology page for the full caveats.

Is Bablake safe at night?

At night, Bablake is rated as relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Coventry. If you're unsure, it's worth checking recent local reviews for your specific street or block, since a neighbourhood-wide rating can't capture block-by-block variation.

Is Bablake a good area to stay in as a tourist?

Bablake's day rating (roughly average compared to other neighbourhoods in Coventry) is the more relevant one for typical daytime tourist activity; check the night rating too if you'll be out late. Note that the Booking.com link on this page searches Coventry, not Bablake specifically: Booking does not list this neighbourhood as a destination of its own, so check each property's address against the map above.
